title: Enterprise buyer decision profiles: latency-cost-fallback acceptability study
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Synthesize primary research and telemetry to create decision profiles for enterprise buyers that specify acceptable latency bands, cost-per-call thresholds, and fallback tolerances (e.g., model variant substitution, lower-quality quantized models, or regional rerouting). Deliverable: a decision matrix and a short playbook used by PM/Eng/Sales to determine default routing policies and guardrails for Dedicated/Private deployments.
goals: Map 3-4 enterprise buyer personas (platform, product, security, procurement) to explicit latency and cost tolerances
Quantify fallback acceptance rates for each persona (what percentage of calls can fall back to smaller/quantized models or to a different region)
Produce a decision matrix that can be converted to runtime routing policies and a one-page sales checklist
metrics: Primary metric: % of enterprise customers within SLA when applying proposed fallback policies
Secondary metric: estimated change in token unit cost and 95th percentile latency per persona
Research metric: % of interviewees who report willingness to accept fallbacks in at least one scenario
research_plan: 1) Telemetry synthesis: sample 30 enterprise tenants across verticals from Console latency/cost dashboards (span: last 90 days)
2) User interviews: 12 targeted interviews across PLG customers and eight enterprise leads (security, infra, procurement) to surface tolerance thresholds
3) Rapid proto A/B: run canary routing experiment for two weeks on non-critical routes to estimate real fallback acceptance
4) Competitive scan: collect published SLAs and routing fallback policies from 5 competing vendors
interview_questions: What is the maximum 95th percentile latency you consider acceptable for end-user features?
How do you prioritize latency vs. response quality when cost/predictability constraints exist?
Would you accept region-based fallbacks during a primary region outage? Under what conditions?
Are you willing to accept a lower-quality quantized model as a temporary fallback if it reduces cost by >35%?
What business workflows are intolerant of any model substitution (e.g., legal, compliance, audit logs)?
tradeoffs_and_risks: Bias toward permissive fallback policies reduces immediate cost but increases risk of quality regressions and customer confusion
Heavy reliance on canary telemetry may underrepresent peak-time tolerances
Asking procurement teams about micro-level tolerances may yield conservative answers that don't match product team preferences
Implementation complexity: fine-grained per-route routing policies increase operational surface area and testing burden
timeline: Weeks 1-2: Telemetry export and segmentation; recruit interview cohort
Week 3: Conduct interviews and run 2-week canary A/B on non-critical routes
Week 4: Synthesize decision matrix, draft playbook, stakeholder reviews
Week 5: Finalize docs and handoff to Eng for policy prototyping
acceptance_criteria: Decision matrix with persona rows and acceptable latency/cost/fallback columns completed
At least 12 interviews logged with notes and transcripts
Canary experiment results with pre/post metrics and sample traces attached
Playbook one-pager reviewed by Eng and Sales and signed off by PM
